title: P3: SyncUploader engine (idempotent, cursor, backoff)
description: New SyncUploader.swift: ObservableObject on a dedicated serial queue, one default URLSession (NOT background). Algorithm = SYNC_PROTOCOL.md section 8: ensure token (refresh) -> POST devices -> POST sessions -> loop POST samples advancing cursor (sync.cursorSampleID) -> cursor repair via GET sessions/{id} when local state lost. Honor ping.limits cap; over-cap 413 -> halve. Triggers: stopRecording()/endSession() + ScenePhase background/active + backoff retry timer. NEVER triggered from ingest() (1 Hz path). Every error caught into sync.lastResult; recording/DB/UI never affected; no local deletion. Blocked by P1 + P2.

title: Server Sync: push recorded HR to a user-configured server
description:
Add optional, user-configured upload of recorded data to a server implementing the vendor-neutral Server Sync Protocol v1. The app stays a generic public recorder; the server is whatever the user points it at (jmdashboard is the reference impl).

Locked design decisions (see docs/2026-05-19-server-sync-design.md and docs/SYNC_PROTOCOL.md):
- HTTPS only — non-https base URLs rejected; no insecure escape hatch, no ATS exception.
- Full base URL configured in iOS Settings.app + in-app; app appends only relative resource paths; protocol version via X-HRM-Protocol header.
- Auth: OAuth 2.1 preferred (discovered via unauthenticated GET ping -> RFC 8414 metadata; RFC 7591 dynamic client registration; Authorization Code + PKCE S256; refresh token enables unattended background upload), reusing the server's EXISTING authorization server (no HR-specific endpoint). Static Bearer token is the documented fallback for minimal servers.
- Idempotent + incremental: cursor = monotonic samples.id; re-sends safe; cursor repair via GET sessions/{id}.

Hard constraints (CLAUDE.md): live-BPM screen untouched; off by default; memory-light streaming (bounded LIMIT, no buffers); capture 1 Hz hot path never blocked; any sync/auth failure swallowed — recording, the DB, and the UI are never affected and no local data is ever deleted by a sync.

Child phases: 1) SyncSettings+Settings.bundle  2) HRDatabase read-only upload queries  3) SyncAuth (OAuth 2.1 + static fallback)  4) SyncUploader engine  5) ServerSyncView (in-app sign-in/status)  6) reference mock server  7) manual on-device verification  8) version bump.
design: Server side spec: jmdashboard docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-19-heart-rate-ingest-design.md + docs/openapi/openapi-heart-rate-ingest-design.yaml. Wire contract owned by this repo: docs/SYNC_PROTOCOL.md.

title: CSV export: quote rr_ms / text fields (csvEscape unused in streaming path)
description:
Symptom (user-reported, confirmed on a 33.8k-row export): the rr_ms column contains semicolon-joined values like 873;314;387. That part is BY DESIGN — a single GATT 0x2A37 notification can carry multiple R-R intervals, joined with ';' at HRDatabase.swift:184-187. The bug is the CSV is emitted with ZERO quoting/escaping.

Root cause: a csvEscape helper exists (HRDatabase.swift:376, wraps in double-quotes and doubles interior quotes) but the streaming export path (HRDatabase.swift:344) string-interpolates every field raw and never calls it. Verified: 0 double-quote chars in the whole export file.

Impact:
- Portability/corruption: many spreadsheet locales (most of Europe; OS list-separator dependent) use ';' as the CSV delimiter. Opening this file there splits rr_ms (e.g. 873;314;387) into 3 columns and shifts every subsequent column on RR-bearing rows, misaligning the table. ~83% of TICKR rows carry RR, so most of the file misaligns.
- Latent: any text field containing a comma/quote/newline (device_name, manufacturer, model, body_location) would break column alignment too — currently safe only because the sample data has none.

Fix: route all text and sub-delimited fields through the existing csvEscape in the streaming row builder (HRDatabase.swift:344) so output is RFC 4180 compliant; rr_ms in particular must be quoted. Keep the header row consistent (HRDatabase.swift:291). Do NOT change rr_ms internal ';' semantics or the 64KB chunked streaming / queue.sync split. Also document rr_ms semantics in README (semicolon-separated = multiple R-R intervals from one notification, milliseconds).

Out of scope: RR data-quality/artifacts (implausible short intervals like 117ms, 4917ms gaps from the chest strap) — that is sensor noise the app correctly recorded, a separate concern from export formatting.

Verification: exported CSV opens correctly with a ';' list-separator locale; a strict RFC4180 parser round-trips it; every row still resolves to 12 logical columns; rr_ms cell preserved intact as one value.
close_reason: Fixed: CSV export now routes rr_ms through csvEscape (it bypassed it — was string-interpolated raw at the rr field; now uses field(8)), and csvEscape's trigger set gains ';' so a multi-value rr_ms like 873;314;387 is RFC-4180 double-quoted. This keeps it one cell even in ';'-list-separator locales (most of Europe), fixing the column misalignment on the ~83% of RR-bearing rows. Other text fields already routed through field()->csvEscape (now also ;-safe). Internal ';' join semantics, 64KB chunked streaming, and the queue.sync split unchanged; quoting extra fields is valid RFC 4180 so a strict comma parser still round-trips. README documents rr_ms semicolon semantics + that the cell is quoted. Out of scope (per issue): RR data-quality/sensor-noise. xcodebuild iphonesimulator BUILD SUCCEEDED. Version 0.21->0.22, build 1.

title: Allow changing device mid-recording
description:
Let the user switch to a different heart-rate strap without stopping the active recording session. Today select(_:) persists one preferredDeviceUUID and connects; there is no path to swap straps while a session is open, so changing devices means stop -> reconnect -> startRecording (new session, history split).

Behavior: while recording, picking another strap disconnects the current peripheral and connects the new one, and capture continues into the SAME session_id (no sample loss across the swap; reuse the resumeActiveSessionIfNeeded / activeSessionID machinery). Decide UX for the gap while the new strap connects (pause vs. no-contact).

Data-model wrinkle: a session row carries one device identity (device_name + the new manufacturer/model/firmware/body_location columns) and samples carry only session_id, so a mid-session swap makes the session's device fields ambiguous and samples unattributable to the right strap. This is the same per-sample device-identity gap as the multi-device epic — coordinate the schema decision there (related: HRMRecorder-km4). Single-device, no-swap behavior must stay unchanged.
close_reason: Subsumed and delivered by the km4 epic. The original ask — switch/back-up straps without splitting the session — is satisfied because one session now spans multiple straps: connect a backup strap any time (additive picker works while recording, km4.4), both stream into the same session_id with per-sample device attribution (km4.3), and per-strap background reconnect (km4.2 didDisconnect) keeps a backup going if the primary drops. No history split; resumeActiveSessionIfNeeded/activeSessionID unchanged. Connect-gap UX = the existing .connecting/no-contact state (no pause, per plan). Closing as done via km4.

title: Support multiple devices recording at once
description:
Today the app is single-strap by construction: HeartRateManager owns one CBCentralManager + one preferredDeviceUUID, exposes one set of @Published BPM/state, and a session implicitly == one device (samples carry only session_id, no device dimension). Goal: connect to and record from N heart-rate straps simultaneously.

Major work areas (likely child issues):

1. Data model — add a device identity dimension so samples are attributable per device. Either a devices table + samples.device_id, or per-(session,device) rows. Migrate existing DBs (follow the COALESCE/ALTER pattern just added for sessions device-info columns). Update README schema + CSV layout (add a device column).

2. BLE layer — HeartRateManager must track a set of peripherals/connections, per-device subscription to 0x2A37, and per-device @Published state instead of scalars. Preserve the main-thread (queue:nil) threading model and the fire-and-forget insert hot path. Background resilience (willRestoreState, restore identifier, autoConnectOrScan, pending connects) must reconnect ALL remembered straps, not one. preferredDeviceUUID becomes a set; activeSessionID resume logic must cover multiple live connections.

3. UI — DevicePicker becomes multi-select / add-more; main screen shows N live BPMs; per-device connection status; recording start/stop semantics across devices (one shared session vs per-device).

4. Export — CSV must include device identity; per-device and combined export.

Open design question to settle first: one session spanning all devices vs one session per device — this drives the schema. Recommend a spike/decision issue before implementation. Pure single-device behavior must remain the default/unchanged for one strap.
close_reason: Epic complete — all 6 phases shipped (km4.1 schema/CSV, km4.2 multi-peripheral facade, km4.3 per-sample attribution, km4.4 minimal multi-strap UI, km4.5 aggregate Live Activity, km4.6 export device predicate). The app now records from N straps simultaneously into one session, attributes every sample to its source strap, and exports it in a self-describing CSV; single-strap behavior and pre-feature CSV output are byte-identical (NULL device_id COALESCEs to the session identity). Memory-light/main-thread/fire-and-forget constraints preserved. Ships as v0.20. Manual physical-device multi-strap verification still pending (per plan).

The new page hosts the existing ForEach(sessions) with per-session swipe delete (db.deleteSession) and per-session CSV export (db.exportCSV(sessionID:)); decide where 'Export all' (exportCSV(sessionID: nil)) and the delete-all action live (likely the sessions page toolbar).

title: Date-gated export ranges
description:
Allow exporting a date/time range instead of the entire database.

Today CSV export streams every sample (HRDatabase CSV path → 64 KB chunks → temp file → ShareSheet). Add a start/end date picker in the export UI and pass the bounds down so the SQL query filters samples by timestamp (and optionally restricts to sessions overlapping the range). Keep the streaming/chunked write path and the fire-and-forget vs queue.sync split unchanged. Empty-range and start>end should be handled gracefully (no file / disabled action). Default range = full history (current behavior) so existing flow is unaffected.
close_reason: Added optional date-gated CSV export. HRDatabase.exportCSV now takes from/to Date? params (default nil = full history, so existing per-session swipe export and Export-All are unchanged); builds the WHERE clause dynamically with s.ts >= from AND s.ts < to bound parameters, leveraging idx_samples_ts. Streaming/chunked 64KB write path and queue.sync split unchanged. A date-filtered range matching zero samples writes no file and returns nil (graceful empty-range). SessionsView gains a 'Limit to date range' toggle revealing From/To .date DatePickers; bounds are whole calendar days (startOfDay..<startOfDay+1d, end-day inclusive); start>end disables the export button with an inline warning. Verified: xcodebuild iphonesimulator BUILD SUCCEEDED. Per corrected release policy: MARKETING_VERSION 0.13->0.14, CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION reset 8->1.
